title.zh: 卷一百三十五 列傳第七十三: 外國下 高麗 金國語解 官稱 人事 物象 物類 姓氏
title.en: Volume 135 Biographies 73: Foreign Countries 2 - Goryeo, Explanation of the Language of the State of Jin, Official Titles, Human Affairs, Art, Classes of Objects, Family Names
title.raw: 卷一百三十五 列傳第七十三: 外國下 高麗 金國語解 官稱 人事 物象 物類 姓氏 Volume 135 Biographies 73: Foreign Countries 2 - Goryeo, Explanation of the Language of the State of Jin, Official Titles, Human Affairs, Art, Classes of Objects, Family Names

sentences.zh: 外國下

translations.literal: Foreign Countries, Part 2
translations.idiomatic: Foreign Countries (Part 2)

sentences.zh: 高麗國王，王楷。

translations.literal: The king of Goryeo was Wang Kai.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goryeo was Wang Kai.

sentences.zh: 其地鴨綠江以東，曷懶路以南，東南皆至於海。

translations.literal: His territory lay east of the Yalu River and south of the Halin Route; to the southeast it extended to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: His realm stretched east of the Yalu River and south along the Halin Route, reaching the sea in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 自遼時，歲時遣使修貢，事具《遼史》。

translations.literal: Since Liao times, they sent envoys each year to present tribute; the details are recorded in the History of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: From the Liao period onward they sent annual tribute missions; the particulars are given in the History of Liao.

sentences.zh: 唐初，靺鞨有粟末、黑水兩部，皆臣屬於高麗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang, among the Mohe there were the Sumo and Heishui tribes, both of which were subject to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tang, the Mohe were divided into the Sumo and Heishui branches, both subordinate to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 唐滅高麗，粟末保東牟山漸強大，號渤海，姓大氏，有文物禮樂。

translations.literal: When Tang destroyed Goryeo, the Sumo, holding Dongmoushan, gradually grew powerful, styled themselves Bohai, took the surname Da, and possessed culture, rites, and music.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang destroyed Goryeo, the Sumo, entrenched at Dongmoushan, grew steadily stronger, proclaimed the state of Bohai under the Da clan, and cultivated civil institutions, ritual, and music.

sentences.zh: 至唐末稍衰，自後不復有聞。

translations.literal: By the end of Tang they had declined somewhat, and thereafter nothing more was heard of them.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Tang they had waned, and after that they passed from record.

sentences.zh: 金伐遼，渤海來歸，蓋其遺裔也。

translations.literal: When Jin attacked Liao, Bohai came to submit; they were presumably their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin campaigned against Liao, Bohai submitted—likely their descendants.

sentences.zh: 黑水靺鞨居古肅慎地，有山曰白山，蓋長白山，金國之所起焉。

translations.literal: The Heishui Mohe dwelt in the ancient territory of the Sushen; they had a mountain called Baishan, which is Mount Changbai, where the Jin state arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Heishui Mohe lived in the old land of the Sushen; their Mount Baishan is Mount Changbai, the place from which the Jin state sprang.

sentences.zh: 女直雖舊屬高麗，不復相通者久矣。

translations.literal: Although the Jurchens had once been subject to Goryeo, they had long ceased to have contact.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Jurchens had once been under Goryeo, they had long since ceased all contact.

sentences.zh: 及金滅遼，高麗以事遼舊禮稱臣于金。

translations.literal: When Jin destroyed Liao, Goryeo, following the old ceremonial forms used toward Liao, declared themselves subjects of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jin overthrew Liao, Goryeo adopted the same tributary etiquette they had shown Liao and acknowledged Jin as suzerain.

sentences.zh: 初，有醫者善治疾，本高麗人，不知其始自何而來，亦不著其姓名，居女直之完顏部。

translations.literal: At first there was a physician skilled at treating illness; he was originally from Goryeo, but it is not known when he first came or what his name was; he lived in the Wanyan tribe of the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning there was a physician skilled in healing, a native of Goryeo whose origins and name were unknown, who resided among the Wanyan Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 穆宗時戚屬有疾，此醫者診視之，穆宗謂醫者曰：「汝能使此人病癒，則吾遣人送汝歸汝鄉國。

translations.literal: When a kinsman of Emperor Muzong fell ill, this physician examined him. Muzong said to the physician: "If you can cure this person's illness, I will send someone to escort you back to your homeland."
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman of Emperor Muzong fell ill, and this physician attended him. Muzong told the physician, "If you can cure this man, I will have you escorted home to your country."

sentences.zh: 」醫者曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " The physician said: "I will."
translations.idiomatic: The physician replied, "I will."

sentences.zh: 」其人疾果愈，穆宗乃以初約歸之。

translations.literal: " That person's illness was indeed cured, and Muzong then fulfilled his original promise and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: The patient recovered, and Muzong kept his word and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 乙離骨嶺僕散部胡石來勃堇居高麗、女直之兩間，穆宗使族人叟阿招之，因使叟阿送醫者，歸之高麗境上。

translations.literal: Hushilai, a tribal leader of the Pusans in the Yilibone Ridge region, lived between Goryeo and the Jurchens. Muzong sent his clansman Sou'a to summon him, and had Sou'a escort the physician back to the Goryeo border.
translations.idiomatic: Hushilai, a Pusan chieftain of the Yilibone Ridge district, dwelt between Goryeo and the Jurchens. Muzong dispatched his kinsman Sou'a to summon him and had Sou'a escort the physician to the Goryeo frontier.

sentences.zh: 醫者歸至高麗，因謂高麗人，女直居黑水部者部族日強，兵益精悍，年穀屢稔。

translations.literal: When the physician returned to Goryeo, he told the Goryeo people that the Jurchen tribes dwelling in the Heishui region were growing stronger day by day, their troops ever more formidable, and their harvests repeatedly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Goryeo, the physician reported that the Jurchen tribes of the Heishui region were growing daily in strength, their soldiers ever more formidable, and their harvests repeatedly plentiful.

sentences.zh: 高麗王聞之。

translations.literal: The king of Goryeo heard this.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goryeo heard of it.

sentences.zh: 乃通使於女直。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly opened diplomatic contact with the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 既而，胡石來來歸，遂率乙離骨嶺東諸部皆內附。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Hushilai came to submit, and then led all the tribes east of Yilibone Ridge to attach themselves inward.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hushilai submitted, and the tribes east of Yilibone Ridge followed him into Jin allegiance.

sentences.zh: 穆宗十年癸未，阿疏自遼使其徒達紀來說曷懶甸人，曷懶甸人執之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Muzong, guwei (1043), Ashu sent his follower Daji from Liao to win over the Halin district people; the Halin people seized him.
translations.idiomatic: In Muzong's tenth year, guwei (1043), Ashu sent his man Daji from Liao to sway the people of the Halin district, but they seized him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以達紀送高麗，謂高麗王曰：「前此為亂於汝鄙者，皆此輩也。

translations.literal: Muzong sent Daji to Goryeo and said to the king of Goryeo: "Those who have been causing trouble on your borders before were all of this sort."
translations.idiomatic: Muzong handed Daji over to Goryeo, telling the king, "The troublemakers on your frontier have been men of this kind."

sentences.zh: 」及破蕭海里，使斡魯罕往高麗報捷，高麗亦使使來賀。

translations.literal: " After defeating Xiao Haili, he sent Woluhan to Goryeo to report the victory; Goryeo also sent envoys to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Xiao Haili, he sent Woluhan to Goryeo with news of the victory, and Goryeo sent envoys in congratulation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複使斜葛與斡魯罕往聘，高麗王曰：「斜葛，女直之族弟也，其禮有加矣。

translations.literal: Before long he again sent Xiege and Woluhan on a mission of courtesy; the king of Goryeo said: "Xiege is a clansman of the Jurchens, and his reception has been especially generous."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent Xiege and Woluhan again on a friendly mission. The king of Goryeo said, "Xiege is a Jurchen kinsman, and he has been honored with exceptional ceremony."

sentences.zh: 」乃以一大銀盤為謝。

translations.literal: " He then presented a large silver platter in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a large silver platter in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 厥後，曷懶甸諸部盡欲來附，高麗聞之不欲使來附，恐近於己而不利也，使人邀止之。

translations.literal: Thereafter all the tribes of the Halin district wished to come and attach themselves; when Goryeo heard of this they did not wish them to attach themselves, fearing that proximity would not be to their advantage, and sent men to intercept and stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Later every tribe of the Halin district sought to submit. Goryeo, fearing neighbors so close, sent men to block them.

sentences.zh: 斜葛在高麗及往來曷懶道中，具知其事，遂使石適歡往納曷懶甸人。

translations.literal: Xiege, while in Goryeo and traveling the roads to and from Halin, learned the full details of this affair, and therefore sent Shishihuan to go and receive the Halin district people.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege, while in Goryeo and traveling the Halin routes, learned the whole affair and sent Shishihuan to bring the Halin people in.

sentences.zh: 未行而穆宗沒，康宗嗣，遣石適歡以星顯統門之兵往至乙離骨嶺，益募兵趨活涅水，徇地曷懶甸，收叛亡七城。

translations.literal: Before he set out Muzong died and Emperor Kangzong succeeded; he dispatched Shishihuan with troops from the Xingxian Tongmen to proceed to Yilibone Ridge, recruited more troops and pressed toward the Huonie River, pacified the Halin district, and recovered seven cities of deserters.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shishihuan marched, Muzong died and Kangzong succeeded. Kangzong sent him with Xingxian Tongmen troops to Yilibone Ridge, raised more men, advanced to the Huonie River, pacified the Halin district, and recovered seven rebel towns.

sentences.zh: 高麗使人來告曰：「事有當議者。

translations.literal: Goryeo sent envoys to report: "There are matters that ought to be discussed."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent word that certain matters required discussion.

sentences.zh: 」曷懶甸官屬使斜勒詳穩、冶剌保詳穩往，石適歡亦使杯魯往，高麗執冶剌保等，而遣杯魯曰：「無與爾事。

translations.literal: " The officials of the Halin district sent Xiele Xiangwen and Yeliba Xiangwen; Shishihuan also sent Peilu. Goryeo seized Yeliba and the others, and sent Peilu back saying: "This is none of your affair."
translations.idiomatic: Halin officials sent Xiele Xiangwen and Yeliba Xiangwen; Shishihuan sent Peilu as well. Goryeo detained Yeliba and his party and returned Peilu with the message, "This does not concern you."

sentences.zh: 」於是，五水之民皆附於高麗，團練使陷者十四人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the people of the Five Waters all attached themselves to Goryeo, and fourteen regimental commanders were taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Five Waters people all went over to Goryeo, and fourteen regimental commanders were captured.

sentences.zh: 二年甲申，高麗來攻，石適歡大破之，殺獲甚眾，追入其境，焚略其戍守而還。

translations.literal: In the second year, jiashen (1044), Goryeo attacked; Shishihuan inflicted a great defeat on them, killing and capturing in great numbers, pursued them into their territory, burned their garrison posts, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, jiashen (1044), Goryeo attacked. Shishihuan routed them with heavy casualties, pursued into their land, burned their frontier posts, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 四月，高麗複來攻，石適歡以五百人禦于辟登水，複大破之，追入辟登水，逐其殘眾逾境。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Goryeo attacked again; Shishihuan with five hundred men defended at the Bideng River, again inflicted a great defeat, pursued into the Bideng River, and drove their scattered remnants beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Goryeo attacked again. With five hundred men Shishihuan held the Bideng River, won another great victory, pursued into the river, and drove the survivors beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 於是，高麗王曰：「告邊釁者皆官屬祥丹、傍都里、昔畢罕輩也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the king of Goryeo said: "Those who reported border incidents were all officials Xiangdan, Bangduli, Xibihan, and their ilk."
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goryeo then said, "The border provocations were the work of officials Xiangdan, Bangduli, Xibihan, and the like."

sentences.zh: 」十四團練、六路使人在高麗者，皆歸之，遣使來請和。

translations.literal: " The fourteen regimental commanders and the commissioners of the six routes who were in Goryeo all returned, and they sent envoys to request peace.
translations.idiomatic: The fourteen regimental commanders and six-route commissioners held in Goryeo were released, and envoys came to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 遂使斜葛經正疆界，至乙離骨水、曷懶甸活禰水，留之兩月。

translations.literal: He then sent Xiege to rectify the border, reaching the Yilibone River and the Huonie River of the Halin district, and remained there two months.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege was sent to fix the border as far as the Yilibone and Halin Huonie rivers and stayed two months.

sentences.zh: 斜葛不能聽訟，每一事輒至枝蔓，民頗苦之。

translations.literal: Xiege could not adjudicate lawsuits; on every case he would branch into side issues, and the people suffered considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege could not judge cases cleanly; every dispute sprawled into tangents, and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 康宗召斜葛還，而遣石適歡往。

translations.literal: Kangzong summoned Xiege back and sent Shishihuan in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong recalled Xiege and sent Shishihuan instead.

sentences.zh: 石適歡立幕府于三潺水，其嘗陰與高麗往來為亂階者，即正其罪，餘無所問。

translations.literal: Shishihuan established his headquarters at the Sanshan River; those who had secretly maintained contact with Goryeo and stirred up trouble were punished according to their crimes, and the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shishihuan set up headquarters at the Sanshan River, punished those who had secretly dealt with Goryeo and fomented disorder, and questioned no one else.

sentences.zh: 康宗以為能。

translations.literal: Kangzong considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 四年丙戌，高麗使使黑歡方石來賀嗣位，康宗使杯魯報聘，且尋前約，取亡命之民，高麗許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, bingxu (1046), Goryeo sent envoys Heihuan and Fangshi to congratulate the succession; Kangzong sent Peilu on a return mission and to pursue the earlier agreement to recover fugitive subjects; Goryeo agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, bingxu (1046), Goryeo sent Heihuan and Fangshi to congratulate the succession. Kangzong sent Peilu on a return visit to renew the earlier pact to recover fugitives, and Goryeo agreed.

sentences.zh: 曰：「使使至境上受之。

translations.literal: They said: "Let envoys come to the border to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Have your envoys receive them at the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」康宗以為信然，使完顏部阿聒、烏林答部勝昆往境上受之。

translations.literal: " Kangzong believed this sincere and sent Asuo of the Wanyan tribe and Shengkun of the Ulinada tribe to the border to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong took them at their word and sent Wanyan's Asuo and Ulinada's Shengkun to the border to take delivery.

sentences.zh: 康宗畋于馬紀嶺乙只村以待之。

translations.literal: Kangzong went hunting at Yizhi Village on Maji Ridge to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong hunted at Yizhi Village on Maji Ridge to await them.

sentences.zh: 阿聒、勝昆至境上，高麗遣人殺之，而出兵曷懶甸，築九城。

translations.literal: When Asuo and Shengkun reached the border, Goryeo sent men to kill them and dispatched troops into the Halin district, building nine fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: At the frontier Goryeo killed Asuo and Shengkun, marched into the Halin district, and built nine forts.

sentences.zh: 康宗歸，眾鹹曰：「不可舉兵也，恐遼人將以罪我。

translations.literal: When Kangzong returned, everyone said: "We must not raise troops, lest the Liao people blame us."
translations.idiomatic: On his return everyone urged, "Do not raise troops, lest Liao hold us accountable."

sentences.zh: 」太祖獨曰：「若不舉兵，豈止失曷懶甸，諸部皆非吾有也。

translations.literal: The Taizu alone said: "If we do not raise troops, we will lose not only the Halin district—all the tribes will no longer be ours."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu alone said, "If we do not fight, we lose more than Halin—every tribe will slip from our grasp."

sentences.zh: 」康宗以為然，乃使斡塞將兵伐之，大破高麗兵。

translations.literal: Kangzong thought this correct and sent Wansai to lead troops against them, inflicting a great defeat on the Goryeo army.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong agreed and sent Wansai, who crushed the Goryeo force.

sentences.zh: 六月，高麗率眾來戰，斡塞敗之，進圍其城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Goryeo led their masses to battle; Wansai defeated them and advanced to besiege their city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Goryeo came in force; Wansai defeated them and besieged their city.

sentences.zh: 七月，高麗複請和，康宗曰：「事若酌中，則與之和。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Goryeo again requested peace; Kangzong said: "If the terms are balanced, make peace with them."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Goryeo sued for peace again. Kangzong said, "If the terms are fair, accept peace."

sentences.zh: 」高麗許歸亡入之民，罷九城之戍，複所侵故地，遂與之和。

translations.literal: Goryeo agreed to return the fugitive subjects, abandon the garrisons of the nine cities, and restore the invaded former territory, and peace was made.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo promised to return fugitives, dismantle the nine forts, and restore seized lands, and peace was concluded.

sentences.zh: 收國元年九月，太祖已克黃龍府，命加古撒喝攻保州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Shouguo (1117), after the Taizu had taken Huanglong Prefecture, he ordered Jagusa to attack Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Shouguo 1 (1117), after Taizu had taken Huanglong Prefecture, he ordered Jagusa to attack Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 保州近高麗，遼侵高麗置保州。

translations.literal: Baozhou was near Goryeo; Liao had invaded Goryeo and established Baozhou there.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhou lay near Goryeo; Liao had seized it from Goryeo and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 至是，命撒喝取之，久不下，撒喝請濟師，且言高麗王將遣使來。

translations.literal: At this time he ordered Sagua to take it; after a long time it would not fall; Sagua requested reinforcements and also reported that the king of Goryeo was about to send envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Now Sagua was told to take it. The siege dragged on; he asked for reinforcements and reported that the Goryeo king might send envoys.

sentences.zh: 太祖使納合烏蠢以百騎益之，詔撒喝曰：「汝領偏師，屢破重敵，多所俘獲，及聞胡沙數戰有功，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Nahe Wuchan with a hundred horsemen to reinforce him and instructed Sagua: "You command a detached force and have repeatedly broken strong enemies and taken many captives; when I heard that Husha had fought well in several battles, I was greatly pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Nahe Wuchan with a hundred cavalry and told Sagua, "You lead a detached column, have repeatedly broken strong foes, and taken many captives; I was greatly pleased to hear Husha distinguished himself in battle."

sentences.zh: 若保州未下，但守邊戍，吾已克黃龍府，聞遼主且至，俟破大敵複益汝兵。

translations.literal: If Baozhou is not yet taken, simply guard the border posts; I have already taken Huanglong Prefecture and hear the Liao ruler is coming—after we defeat the main enemy I will reinforce you further.
translations.idiomatic: If Baozhou still holds, hold the frontier; I have taken Huanglong and hear the Liao emperor approaches—after the main battle I will send more troops.

sentences.zh: 所言高麗遣使事，未知果否，至則護送以來。

translations.literal: As for the matter of Goryeo sending envoys, it is not yet known whether it is true; when they arrive, escort them here.
translations.idiomatic: Whether Goryeo truly sends envoys is uncertain; if they come, escort them to me.

sentences.zh: 邊境之事，慎之毋忽。

translations.literal: Border affairs—be careful and do not neglect them.
translations.idiomatic: Guard the frontier carefully and neglect nothing.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，系遼女直麻懣太彎等十五人皆降，攻開州取之，盡降保州諸部女直。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, fifteen persons including the Liao Jurchen Mamantaiwan all surrendered; they attacked and took Kaizhou, and all the Jurchen tribes of Baozhou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month fifteen Liao Jurchens including Mamantaiwan surrendered; Kaizhou was taken and every Jurchen tribe of Baozhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 太祖以撒喝為保州路都統。

translations.literal: The Taizu appointed Sagua commander-in-chief of the Baozhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu made Sagua supreme commander of the Baozhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 太祖已破走遼主軍，撒喝破合主、順化二城，複請濟師攻保州，使斡魯以甲士千人往。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had routed the Liao ruler's army, Sagua took the two cities of Hezhu and Shunhua and again requested reinforcements to attack Baozhou; Wolu was sent with a thousand armored troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu had routed the Liao emperor's army, Sagua took Hezhu and Shunhua and again asked for troops against Baozhou; Wolu went with a thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 二年閏月，高麗遣使來賀捷，且曰：「保州本吾舊地，願以見還。

translations.literal: In the intercalary second month of the second year, Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate the victory and said: "Baozhou was originally our old territory; we wish it returned."
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary second month of year 2, Goryeo congratulated the victory and said, "Baozhou was ours; we ask that it be returned."

sentences.zh: 」太祖謂使者曰：「爾其自取之。

translations.literal: The Taizu said to the envoys: "Take it yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told the envoys, "Take it yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」詔撒喝、烏蠢等曰：「若高麗來取保州，益以胡剌古、習顯等軍備之，或欲合兵，無得輒往，但謹守邊戍。

translations.literal: He instructed Sagua, Wuchan, and the others: "If Goryeo comes to take Baozhou, reinforce them with the armies of Hulagu, Xixian, and the rest; if they wish to join forces, do not go rashly—only hold the border posts carefully."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Sagua and Wuchan, "If Goryeo comes for Baozhou, reinforce them with Hulagu, Xixian, and the rest; if they want joint action, do not rush in—only hold the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」及撒喝、阿實賚等攻保州，遼守將遁去，而高麗兵已在城中。

translations.literal: When Sagua, Ashizhen, and the others attacked Baozhou, the Liao garrison commander fled, but Goryeo troops were already inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Sagua and Ashizhen attacked Baozhou, the Liao commander fled, but Goryeo troops were already in the city.

sentences.zh: 既而，高麗國王使蒲馬請保州，詔諭高麗王曰：「保州近爾邊境，聽爾自取，今乃勤我師徒，破敵城下。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter the king of Goryeo sent Puma to request Baozhou; an edict informed the king of Goryeo: "Baozhou lies near your border and we allowed you to take it yourselves; now you have mobilized our troops to break the enemy beneath their walls."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Goryeo king sent Puma to ask for Baozhou. The edict read, "Baozhou borders you and we let you take it yourself; now you have drawn our army to fight beneath its walls."

sentences.zh: 且蒲馬止是口陳，俟有表請，即當別議。」

translations.literal: Moreover Puma only stated this orally; when there is a formal memorial requesting it, we will discuss the matter separately."
translations.idiomatic: Puma spoke only by mouth; when a formal petition arrives, we shall decide separately."

sentences.zh: 天輔二年十二月，詔諭高麗國王曰：「朕始興師伐遼，已嘗佈告，賴皇天助順，屢敗敵兵，北自上京，南至於海，其間京府州縣部族人民悉皆撫定。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Tianfu (1118), an edict informed the king of Goryeo: "When I first raised troops to attack Liao, I had already proclaimed it; relying on Heaven's assistance in accord with righteousness, we repeatedly defeated the enemy; from Shangjing in the north to the sea in the south, among capital districts, prefectures, counties, tribes, and people in between, all have been pacified."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tianfu 2 (1118), an edict told the Goryeo king, "When I first marched against Liao I proclaimed my intent; Heaven aided the righteous cause and we repeatedly defeated the foe; from Shangjing north to the sea south, every capital, prefecture, county, tribe, and people between have been settled."

sentences.zh: 今遣孛堇朮孛報諭，仍賜馬一匹，至可領也。」

translations.literal: Now I send the commander Zhu Bao to report and inform you, and also bestow one horse, which you may receive."
translations.idiomatic: I now send Commander Zhu Bao to notify you and grant one horse for you to accept."

sentences.zh: 三年，高麗增築長城三尺，邊吏發兵止之，弗從，報曰：「修補舊城。

translations.literal: In the third year, Goryeo added three feet to the height of the Great Wall; border officials sent troops to stop them; they did not obey and reported: "We are repairing the old wall."
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Goryeo raised the Great Wall three feet. Border officials sent troops to stop them; they refused, saying they were repairing the old wall.

sentences.zh: 」曷懶甸孛堇胡剌古、習顯以聞，詔曰：「毋得侵軼生事，但慎固營壘，廣布耳目而已。」

translations.literal: The Halin district commander Hulagu and Xixian reported this; an edict said: "Do not encroach or stir up trouble; only strengthen your camps and posts and spread scouts widely."
translations.idiomatic: Halin commanders Hulagu and Xixian reported it. The edict said, "Do not raid or provoke; only fortify camps and extend scouts."

sentences.zh: 四年，咸州路都統司以兵分屯於保州、畢里圍二城，請益兵，詔曰：「汝等分列屯戍，以固封守，甚善。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Xianzhou Circuit commander-in-chief's office stationed troops separately at Baozhou and Biliwei cities and requested more troops; an edict said: "You are posted separately to garrison and solidify the frontier defense—very good."
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 the Xianzhou circuit headquarters divided troops between Baozhou and Biliwei and asked for reinforcements. The edict said, "Separate garrisons to secure the border—well done."

sentences.zh: 高麗累世臣事於遼，或有交通，可常遣人偵伺。」

translations.literal: Goryeo for generations were subjects of Liao; they may have communications—regularly send men to spy on them."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo served Liao for generations; they may still communicate—send scouts regularly."

sentences.zh: 使習顯以獲遼國州郡諭高麗，其國方誅亂者，使謂習顯曰：「此與先父國王之書。

translations.literal: Xixian was sent to inform Goryeo of the Liao prefectures and districts captured; their state was just executing rebels, and they had Xixian told: "This is a letter from my late father's reign."
translations.idiomatic: Xixian was sent to tell Goryeo of captured Liao prefectures. The court was executing rebels; they told Xixian, "This is a letter from my late father's reign."

sentences.zh: 」習顯就館。

translations.literal: Xixian went to the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Xixian went to the lodge.

sentences.zh: 凡誅戮官僚七十余人，即依舊禮接見，而以表來賀，並貢方物。

translations.literal: In all more than seventy officials were executed; they then received him according to the old ceremonial forms, and he presented a memorial of congratulation together with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy officials were executed; he was then received under the old forms, presented a congratulatory memorial, and sent local tribute.

sentences.zh: 複以遼帝亡入夏國報之。

translations.literal: They also reported that the Liao emperor had fled into the Xia state.
translations.idiomatic: They also reported that the Liao emperor had fled into Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 高隨、斜野奉使高麗，至境上，接待之禮不遜，隨等不敢往，太宗曰：「高麗世臣於遼，當以事遼之禮事我，而我國有新喪，遼主未獲，勿遽強之。

translations.literal: Gao Sui and Xieye were sent as envoys to Goryeo; when they reached the border the reception was not deferential, and Sui and the others did not dare proceed. Emperor Taizong said: "Goryeo for generations were subjects of Liao; they should treat us with the ceremonial forms used toward Liao, but our state has a fresh bereavement and the Liao ruler has not yet been captured—do not press them hastily."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sui and Xieye were sent to Goryeo; at the frontier the reception was disrespectful and they dared not enter. Taizong said, "Goryeo long served Liao and should treat us with Liao etiquette, but we mourn a new death and the Liao emperor is not yet taken—do not press them."

sentences.zh: 」命高隨等還。

translations.literal: He ordered Gao Sui and the others to return.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gao Sui and his party to return.

sentences.zh: 天會二年，同知南路都統鶻實答奏，高麗納叛亡、增邊備，必有異圖。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhui (1124), Tongzhi of the Southern Route Army reported that Goryeo had harbored deserters and strengthened border defenses, and must have ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 2 (1124), the southern route deputy reported Goryeo sheltering fugitives and strengthening defenses, surely with hostile intent.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「凡有通問，毋違常式。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In all communications, do not depart from the regular forms.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "In all exchanges keep to established protocol.

sentences.zh: 或來侵略，則整爾行列與之從事。

translations.literal: If they come to invade, then array your ranks and engage them.
translations.idiomatic: If they invade, form your ranks and fight.

sentences.zh: 敢先犯彼者，雖捷必罰。

translations.literal: Whoever first attacks the other, though victorious shall be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever strikes first, though victorious, will be punished."

sentences.zh: 」詔闍母以甲士千人戍海島，以備之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chanmu to garrison the sea islands with a thousand armored troops as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: Chanmu was ordered to garrison the sea islands with a thousand armored men as precaution.

sentences.zh: 四年，國王王楷遣使奉表稱籓，優詔答之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, King Wang Kai sent envoys presenting a memorial declaring himself a vassal; a gracious edict replied.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 King Wang Kai sent a memorial declaring vassalage; a gracious edict answered.

sentences.zh: 上使高伯淑、烏至忠使高麗，凡遣使往來當盡循遼舊，仍取保州路及邊地人口在彼界者，須盡數發還。

translations.literal: The court sent Gao Boshu and Wuzhi Zhong as envoys to Goryeo; all missions going back and forth should fully follow Liao precedent, and also recover the population of Baozhou Circuit and the border districts who were on their side—all must be sent back in full.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Gao Boshu and Wuzhi Zhong to Goryeo. All missions were to follow Liao precedent and recover every Baozhou and border subject on their side.

sentences.zh: 敕伯淑曰：「若一一聽從，即以保州地賜之。

translations.literal: He instructed Boshu: "If they comply in every particular, then grant them the territory of Baozhou."
translations.idiomatic: Boshu was told, "If they obey on every point, grant them Baozhou."

sentences.zh: 」高伯淑至高麗，王楷附表謝，一依事遼舊制。

translations.literal: When Gao Boshu reached Goryeo, Wang Kai appended a memorial of thanks, fully following the old forms used toward Liao.
translations.idiomatic: At Goryeo Wang Kai added a memorial of thanks, fully following Liao forms.

sentences.zh: 八年，楷上表，乞免索保州亡入邊戶。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Kai presented a memorial requesting exemption from demanding the fugitive border households of Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Kai petitioned to be excused from reclaiming Baozhou fugitives on the border.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高麗十人捕魚，大風飄其船抵海岸，曷蘇館人獲之，詔還其國。

translations.literal: That year ten Goryeo men were fishing when a great wind blew their boat to the shore; Yasu guan people seized them, and an edict ordered them returned to their country.
translations.idiomatic: That year ten Goryeo fishermen were blown ashore; Yasuguan people seized them and an edict returned them home.

sentences.zh: 既而勖上表請不索保州亡入高麗戶口，太宗從之，自是保州封域始定。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Xu presented a memorial requesting not to demand the Baozhou fugitives who had entered Goryeo; Taizong assented, and from this time the borders of Baozhou were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu petitioned not to reclaim Baozhou fugitives in Goryeo; Taizong agreed, and Baozhou's borders were fixed.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，詔加楷開府儀同三司、上柱國。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong (1142), an edict added to Kai the titles of Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Shangzhuguo.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 (1142) Kai was given Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Shangzhuguo.

sentences.zh: 六年，楷薨，子晛嗣立。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Kai died and his son Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Kai died and his son Xian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，鴨綠江堡戍頗被侵越焚毀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading (1164), the garrison fortresses on the Yalu River were repeatedly invaded, burned, and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 4 (1164) Yalu River garrison forts suffered repeated raids and burning.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，世宗因正旦使朝辭，諭之曰：「邊境小小不虞，爾主使然邪，疆吏為之邪？

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, when the New Year's envoys took leave, Shizong instructed them: "Were these small border incidents caused by your lord, or by frontier officials?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 5, as New Year envoys took leave, Shizong told them, "Were these small border troubles your king's doing or his officers'?

sentences.zh: 若果疆吏為之，爾主亦當懲戒之也。

translations.literal: If it was indeed the frontier officials, your lord should punish them as well."
translations.idiomatic: If his officers did it, your king should punish them too."

sentences.zh: 」初，高麗使者別有私進禮物以為常，是歲萬春節，上以使者私進不應典禮，詔罷之。

translations.literal: Previously Goryeo envoys had separately presented private gifts as a regular practice; that year at the Ten Thousand Springs festival the court considered the envoys' private gifts not in accord with proper ceremony and ordered them stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo envoys had habitually offered private gifts aside from tribute; that Ten Thousand Springs festival the court ruled these improper and abolished them.

sentences.zh: 十年，王晛弟翼陽公皓廢晛自立。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Wang Xian's younger brother the Duke of Yiyang, Hao, deposed Xian and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Wang Xian's younger brother Duke Hao of Yiyang deposed Xian and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 十月，賜生日使、大宗正丞颭至界上，高麗邊吏稱前王已讓位，不肯受使者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the birthday envoy, Grand Director of the Imperial Clan Zheng, reached the border; Goryeo border officials said the former king had already abdicated and refused to receive the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month birthday envoy Zheng of the Imperial Clan Directorate reached the border; Goryeo officials said the former king had abdicated and would not receive him.

sentences.zh: 十一年三月，王皓以讓國來奏告，詔婆速路勿受，有司移文詳問。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eleventh year, Wang Hao came to report his abdication of the state; an edict ordered the Bian Su circuit not to receive him, and the relevant office sent documents for detailed inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 11 Wang Hao came to announce his succession; an edict told Bian Su circuit not to receive him and the ministry sent documents for full inquiry.

sentences.zh: 高麗告曰：「前王久病，昏耄不治，以母弟皓權攝國事。

translations.literal: Goryeo reported: "The former king has long been ill, senile and unable to govern, and his younger brother Hao by the same mother has been entrusted to administer state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo reported that the former king had long been ill, senile and unfit to rule, and that his uterine younger brother Hao was acting as regent.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「讓國大事也，何以不先陳請。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Abdication of the state is a great matter—why was it not reported and requested beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Surrendering the throne is a grave affair—why was it not announced in advance?"

sentences.zh: 」詔有司再詳問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to inquire again in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministries to investigate further.

sentences.zh: 高麗乃以王晛讓國表來，大略稱先臣楷遺訓傳位於弟，又言其子有罪不可立之意。

translations.literal: Goryeo then sent Wang Xian's memorial of abdication; in general it stated that the late subject Kai's testamentary instruction was to pass the throne to his younger brother, and also expressed that his son was guilty and unfit to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo then sent Wang Xian's abdication memorial, claiming Kai's deathbed wish to pass the throne to his brother and that his son was unworthy to succeed.

sentences.zh: 上疑之，以問宰執，丞相良弼奏曰：「此不可信。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious and asked the chief ministers; Chancellor Liang Bi memorialized: "This cannot be believed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was doubtful and consulted his ministers. Chancellor Liang Bi said, "This cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 晛止一子，往年生孫，嘗有表自陳生孫之喜，一也。

translations.literal: Xian has only one son; in a previous year a grandson was born, and he once presented a memorial expressing joy at the birth of a grandson—that is the first point."
translations.idiomatic: First, Xian has only one son; he once memorialized rejoicing at a grandson's birth."

sentences.zh: 皓嘗作亂，晛囚之，二也。

translations.literal: Hao once made rebellion and Xian imprisoned him—that is the second point."
translations.idiomatic: Second, Hao once rebelled and Xian imprisoned him."

sentences.zh: 今晛不遣使，皓乃遣使，三也。

translations.literal: Now Xian does not send envoys while Hao does—that is the third point."
translations.idiomatic: Third, Xian sends no envoys while Hao does."

sentences.zh: 朝廷賜晛生日使，皓不轉達於晛，乃稱未敢奉受，四也。

translations.literal: The court bestowed birthday envoys on Xian, but Hao did not forward them to Xian and instead said he dared not accept them—that is the fourth point."
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the court's birthday envoys for Xian were not forwarded; Hao said he dared not receive them."

sentences.zh: 今皓篡兄誣于天子，安可忍也。

translations.literal: Now Hao has usurped his elder brother and deceived the Son of Heaven—how can this be tolerated."
translations.idiomatic: Hao has seized power from his brother and deceived the throne—this cannot be endured."

sentences.zh: 」右丞孟浩曰：「當詢彼國士民，果皆推服，即當遣使封冊。

translations.literal: Right Vice Chancellor Meng Hao said: "We should inquire of the scholars and people of that country; if they truly all support him, then we may send envoys to invest him with seals."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Chancellor Meng Hao said, "Inquire whether their people truly accept him; only then send investiture envoys."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「封一國之君詢於民眾，此與除拜猛安謀克何異。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "To invest the ruler of a state by inquiring of the populace—how is this different from appointing a Meng'an or Mouke?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Consulting the masses to enfeoff a king is no different from appointing a Meng'an or Mouke."

sentences.zh: 」乃卻其使者，而以詔書詳問王晛，吏部侍郎靖為宣問王晛使。

translations.literal: He therefore sent back their envoys and issued an edict in detailed inquiry to Wang Xian; Vice Minister of Personnel Jing was made envoy to question Wang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected their envoys and sent an edict questioning Wang Xian; Vice Minister Jing was made inquiry envoy.

sentences.zh: 皓實篡國，囚晛於海島。

translations.literal: Hao had in fact usurped the state and imprisoned Xian on a sea island.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had indeed usurped the throne and imprisoned Xian on a sea island.

sentences.zh: 靖至高麗，皓稱王晛已避位出居他所，病加無損，不能就位拜命，往復險遠，非使者所宜往。

translations.literal: When Jing reached Goryeo, Hao said Wang Xian had already yielded the throne and dwelt elsewhere; his illness had worsened without improvement and he could not come to receive the mandate in person; the journey back and forth was perilous and remote and not suitable for an envoy to go.
translations.idiomatic: At Goryeo, Hao said Xian had abdicated and lived elsewhere, was too ill to receive the mandate, and the route was too dangerous for an envoy.

sentences.zh: 靖竟不得見晛，乃以詔授皓，轉取晛表附奏，其言與前表大概相同。

translations.literal: Jing in the end could not see Xian; he therefore presented the edict to Hao, obtained Xian's memorial as an attachment, and its words were roughly the same as the earlier memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jing never saw Xian; he gave the edict to Hao and attached Xian's memorial, which matched the earlier one.

sentences.zh: 靖還，上問大臣，皆曰：「晛表如此，可遂封之。

translations.literal: When Jing returned, the emperor asked the great ministers; all said: "Since Xian's memorial is thus, we may proceed to invest him."
translations.idiomatic: On Jing's return the ministers said Xian's memorial sufficed for investiture.

sentences.zh: 」丞相良弼、平章政事守道曰：「待皓祈請未晚也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Liang Bi and Privy Councillor Shoudao said: "It is not too late to wait until Hao petitions."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Bi and Shoudao urged waiting until Hao himself petitioned.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，皓遣其禮部侍郎張翼明等請封。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Hao sent his Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yiming and others to request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hao sent Zhang Yiming of the Ministry of Rites to request investiture.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，遂賜封冊。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year investiture was then granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 12 investiture was granted.

sentences.zh: 皓生日在正月十九日，是歲十二月將盡，未及遣使，有司請至來歲舉行焉。

translations.literal: Hao's birthday fell on the nineteenth day of the first month; that year the twelfth month was nearly ended and envoys could not be sent in time; the relevant office requested that it be carried out the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's birthday was the nineteenth of the first month; the year was nearly over, so the office asked to defer the birthday mission until the next year.

sentences.zh: 十五年，高麗西京留守趙位寵叛皓，遣徐彥等九十六人上表曰：「前王本非避讓，大將軍鄭沖夫、郎將李義方實弑之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Zhao Weichong, military commissioner of Goryeo's Western Capital, rebelled against Hao and sent Xu Yan and ninety-six others with a memorial stating: "The former king did not in fact yield the throne; Grand General Zheng Chongfu and Colonel Li Yifang truly assassinated him."
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 Zhao Weichong, Goryeo's Western Capital commissioner, rebelled and sent Xu Yan and ninety-six men claiming the former king had not abdicated but was murdered by Zheng Chongfu and Li Yifang.

sentences.zh: 臣位寵請以慈悲嶺以西至鴨綠江四十餘城內屬，請兵助援。

translations.literal: Your subject Weichong requests that the territory from Cibei Ridge west to the Yalu River—more than forty cities—be brought within [your rule], and asks for troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Weichong asked that more than forty cities from Cibei Ridge west to the Yalu be annexed and troops sent to aid him.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「王皓已加封冊，位寵輒敢稱兵為亂，且欲納土，朕懷撫萬邦，豈助叛臣為虐。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wang Hao has already received investiture; Weichong dares to raise troops in rebellion and moreover wishes to offer territory—I cherish and comfort the myriad states; how could I aid a rebel minister in his cruelty."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Hao is already invested; Weichong rebels and offers land—I comfort all realms and will not aid a rebel."

sentences.zh: 」詔執徐彥等送高麗。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xu Yan and the others seized and sent to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Xu Yan and his party to Goryeo in custody.

sentences.zh: 頃之，王皓定趙位寵之亂，遣使奏謝，自位寵之亂，皓所遣生日回謝、橫賜回謝、賀正旦、進奉、萬春節等使，皆阻不通，至是，皓並奏之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Wang Hao settled Zhao Weichong's rebellion and sent envoys to report thanks; since Weichong's rebellion, the birthday return-thanks envoys, horizontal-gift return-thanks envoys, New Year's envoys, tribute envoys, and Ten Thousand Springs festival envoys that Hao had sent were all blocked and could not pass—now Hao reported all of this together.
translations.idiomatic: Hao soon suppressed Weichong and sent thanks; he also reported that birthday, gift, New Year, tribute, and festival missions had all been blocked during the revolt.

sentences.zh: 詔答其意，其合遣人使令節次入朝。

translations.literal: An edict answered his meaning, and those envoys who ought to be sent were to enter court in proper sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged this and ordered the proper missions to resume in turn.

sentences.zh: 十七年，賀正旦禮物，玉帶乃石似玉者，有司請移問，上曰：「彼小國無能識者，誤以為玉耳，不必移問。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, among the New Year's gifts the jade belt was stone resembling jade; the relevant office requested a diplomatic note of inquiry; the emperor said: "They are a small state without ability to distinguish; they mistakenly took it for jade—there is no need for a note of inquiry."
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 their New Year gift included a stone belt mistaken for jade. The office wanted to inquire; the emperor said the small state could not tell jade from stone and no note was needed.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十二月，有司奏高麗下節押馬官順成例外將帶甲三過界，上以使人所坐罪重，但令發還本國而已。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the relevant office reported that Goryeo's escort officer Shuncheng, in violation of regulations, led armed men across the border three times; the emperor considered the envoy's offense grave but only ordered them sent back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the office reported Goryeo's escort Shuncheng had thrice led armed men across the border illegally; though the offense was grave, they were only sent home.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，皓母任氏薨，皓乞免賜生日及賀謝等事，詔從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Hao's mother Lady Ren died; Hao requested exemption from birthday gifts and congratulatory thanks and the like; an edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 Hao's mother Lady Ren died; he asked to suspend birthday and congratulatory missions and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，皓表自陳衰病，以國讓其弟镡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an, Hao presented a memorial stating his own decline and illness and yielded the state to his younger brother Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 2 Hao memorialized that he was aged and ill and yielded the throne to his brother Chan.

sentences.zh: 镡權國事。

translations.literal: Chan administered state affairs as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Chan acted as regent.

sentences.zh: 是歲，皓廢，镡嗣立。

translations.literal: That year Hao was deposed and Chan succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hao was deposed and Chan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年正月乙丑朔，高麗傔人以小佩刀割梨廡下巡廊，奉職見而糾之，詔館伴官自今前期移文禁止。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month, yichou, of the fourth year of Taihe, Goryeo attendants used small waist-knives to cut pears beneath the corridor of the side hall on their patrol; a palace attendant saw this and reported it; an edict ordered the hosting officials that from now on they should send advance documents forbidding this.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Taihe 4, Goryeo attendants cut pears in the side corridor with small knives; an attendant reported it and hosting officials were told to forbid it by advance notice.

sentences.zh: 是歲，王镡薨，子韺嗣立。

translations.literal: That year Wang Chan died and his son Yin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Chan died and his son Yin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年正月，是時用兵伐宋，夏亦有故，獨高麗遣正旦使，詔不賜曲宴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year of Taihe, at that time troops were being used to attack Song and Xia also had affairs of their own; Goryeo alone sent New Year's envoys; an edict ordered that the curved banquet not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taihe 7, while campaigning against Song and Xia had their own troubles, only Goryeo sent New Year envoys; the curved banquet was withheld.

sentences.zh: 及天壽節，夏、高麗使者皆在，有司奏：「大定初，宋未請和，夏、高麗使者賜曲宴，今請依大定故事。

translations.literal: At the Heavenly Longevity festival, envoys from Xia and Goryeo were both present; the relevant office memorialized: "At the beginning of Dading, when Song had not yet sought peace, envoys from Xia and Goryeo were granted curved banquets; now we request following the Dading precedent."
translations.idiomatic: At the Heavenly Longevity festival both Xia and Goryeo envoys were present; the office asked to follow the Dading precedent of granting curved banquets.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict assented.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年八月，王祦薨，嗣子未行起複。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhi'ning, Wang Yin died; the heir had not yet begun mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhi'ning 1 Wang Yin died before the heir had begun mourning.

sentences.zh: 九月，宣宗即位，邊吏奏：「高麗牒稱，嗣子未起複，不可以凶服迎吉詔，又不可以草土名銜署表。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, when Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, border officials reported: "Goryeo sent a dispatch stating that the heir has not begun mourning leave and cannot receive auspicious edicts in mourning garb, nor sign memorials with the title of one in rough mourning."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Xuanzong's border officers reported Goryeo's dispatch: the heir had not begun mourning and could not receive auspicious edicts in mourning dress or sign memorials as one in rough hemp.

sentences.zh: 」禮官議：「人臣不以私恩廢公義，宜權用吉服迎詔，署表用權國事名銜。

translations.literal: The ritual officials deliberated: "A subject must not abandon public duty for private affection; he should temporarily use auspicious dress to receive the edict and sign memorials with the title of one administering state affairs as regent."
translations.idiomatic: The ritualists ruled that private grief must not override public duty: he should temporarily wear auspicious dress, receive the edict, and sign as regent.

sentences.zh: 俟高麗告哀使至闕，然後遣使致祭、慰問及行封冊。

translations.literal: When Goryeo's mourning announcement envoys reach the court, then envoys may be sent to offer sacrifice, condolences, and perform investiture."
translations.idiomatic: After Goryeo's mourning envoys arrive, the court may send sacrifice, condolence, and investiture missions."

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: The decision was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，宣宗遷汴，遼東道路不通，興定三年，遼東行省奏高麗複有奉表朝貢之意，宰臣奏：「可令行省受其表章，其朝貢之禮俟他日徐議。

translations.literal: The following year Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian; the eastern Liao route was impassable. In the third year of Xingding, the Eastern Liao Branch reported that Goryeo again had the intention to present memorials and tribute; the chief ministers memorialized: "The Branch may be ordered to receive their memorials; the ceremonial tribute may be discussed slowly on another day."
translations.idiomatic: The next year Xuanzong moved to Bian and the eastern route was cut. In Xingding 3 Eastern Liao reported Goryeo wished to resume tribute; ministers said the branch could accept memorials but defer full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」宣宗以為然，乃遣使撫諭高麗，終以道路不通，未遑迎迓，詔行省且羈縻勿絕其好，然自是不復通問矣。

translations.literal: Xuanzong thought this correct and therefore sent envoys to comfort and instruct Goryeo; in the end, because the roads were impassable, there was no leisure to welcome them; an edict ordered the Branch for the time being to keep them attached and not cut off friendly relations—yet from this time exchanges ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong agreed and sent comforting envoys, but the roads remained blocked; the branch was told to keep ties without cutting them off—yet contact effectively ended.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金人本出鞨靺之附於高麗者，始通好為鄰國，既而為君臣，貞祐以後道路不通，僅一再見而已。

translations.literal: Commentary: The Jin people originally came from the Mohe who had attached themselves to Goryeo; at first they opened friendly relations as neighboring states, then became lord and subject; after Zhenyou the roads were impassable and they were seen only once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Jin arose from Mohe once subject to Goryeo; they began as neighbors, became lord and vassal, and after Zhenyou were barely seen again.

sentences.zh: 入聖朝猶子孫相傳自為治，故不復備論，論其與金事相涉者焉。

translations.literal: Under the Sagely Dynasty they still govern themselves in succession from father to son, and therefore are not discussed further here; only matters involving Jin are discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the present dynasty they still rule in hereditary succession and need no full account here; only affairs touching Jin are treated.

sentences.zh: 金國語解

translations.literal: Explanation of the Language of the State of Jin
translations.idiomatic: Explanation of the Jin State Language

sentences.zh: 今文《尚書》辭多奇澀，蓋亦當世之方言也。

translations.literal: The present text of the Documents is full of strange obscurities, for it too is largely the dialect of that age.
translations.idiomatic: The received Book of Documents is often obscure because much of it too is the dialect of its age.

sentences.zh: 《金史》所載本國之語，得諸重譯，而可解者何可闕焉。

translations.literal: The native language recorded in the History of Jin, obtained through repeated translation, has terms that can be understood—how could these be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The native terms in the History of Jin, passed through repeated translation, include many we can still parse and must not omit.

sentences.zh: 若其臣僚之小字，或以賤，或以疾，猶有古人尚質之風，不可文也。

translations.literal: As for the pet names of officials, some denoting baseness or illness, there is still the ancient preference for plain speech that cannot be made literary.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' pet names, marking low birth or illness, preserve an ancient plain style that should not be polished away.

sentences.zh: 國姓為某，漢姓為某，後魏孝文以來已有之矣。

translations.literal: The national surname was such-and-such, the Han surname such-and-such—since Emperor Xiaowen of Later Wei this has already existed.
translations.idiomatic: National clan names and Han surnames have coexisted since Emperor Xiaowen of Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 存諸篇終，以備考索。

translations.literal: They are preserved at the end of the chapters for reference and search.
translations.idiomatic: They are kept at chapters' ends for reference.

sentences.zh: 都勃極烈，總治官名，猶漢云「冢宰」。

translations.literal: Dubojilie: the title of the supreme governing officer, like the Han term "Grand Minister."
translations.idiomatic: Dubojilie: supreme governing title, equivalent to the Han "Grand Minister."

sentences.zh: 諳版勃極烈，官之尊且貴者。

translations.literal: Anban Bojilie: an office both honored and exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Anban Bojilie: a most honored and exalted office.

sentences.zh: 國論勃極烈，尊禮優崇得自由者。

translations.literal: Guolun Bojilie: one honored and exalted with freedom of action.
translations.idiomatic: Guolun Bojilie: one honored with exceptional freedom.

sentences.zh: 胡魯勃極烈，統領官之稱。

translations.literal: Hulu Bojilie: the title of a commanding officer.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Bojilie: title of a commanding officer.

sentences.zh: 移賚勃極烈，位第三曰「移賚」。

translations.literal: Yisai Bojilie: third in rank, called "Yisai."
translations.idiomatic: Yisai Bojilie: third rank, called Yisai.

sentences.zh: 阿買勃極烈，治城邑者。

translations.literal: Amai Bojilie: one who administers cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: Amai Bojilie: administrator of cities and towns.

sentences.zh: 乙室勃極烈，迎邪之官。

translations.literal: Yishi Bojilie: an office for receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: Yishi Bojilie: office for receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 劄失哈勃極烈，守官署之稱。

translations.literal: Zhashiha Bojilie: the title of one who guards government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhashiha Bojilie: guardian of government offices.

sentences.zh: 昃勃極烈，陰陽之官。

translations.literal: Ze Bojilie: an office of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Ze Bojilie: office of yin-yang affairs.

sentences.zh: 迭勃極烈，倅貳之職。

translations.literal: Die Bojilie: the duty of a deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Die Bojilie: deputy's post.

sentences.zh: 猛安，千夫長。

translations.literal: Meng'an: commander of a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an: commander of a thousand.

sentences.zh: 謀克，百夫長也。

translations.literal: Mouke: commander of a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Mouke: commander of a hundred.

sentences.zh: 諸颭「詳穩」，邊戍之官。

translations.literal: Among the various circuits, "Xiangwen": a frontier garrison officer.
translations.idiomatic: Among frontier circuits, Xiangwen: border garrison officer.

sentences.zh: 諸「移里堇」，部落墟砦之首領。

translations.literal: Among the various "Yilijin": chiefs of tribal stockades and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: Yilijin: chiefs of tribal stockades.

sentences.zh: 詳穩、移里堇，本遼語，金人因之而稍異同焉。

translations.literal: Xiangwen and Yilijin were originally Liao terms; the Jin adopted them with slight differences.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwen and Yilijin were Liao terms adopted by Jin with slight changes.

sentences.zh: 禿里，掌部落詞訟，察非違者。

translations.literal: Tuli: in charge of tribal lawsuits, investigating violations.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli: handled tribal litigation and detected violations.

sentences.zh: 烏魯古，牧圉之官。

translations.literal: Ulugu: an office of herds and enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: Ulugu: superintendent of herds.

sentences.zh: 斡里朵，官府治事之所。

translations.literal: Woliduo: the place where the government conducts affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Woliduo: seat of government business.

sentences.zh: 孛論出，胚胎之名。

translations.literal: Belunchu: the name for an embryo.
translations.idiomatic: Belunchu: term for an embryo.

sentences.zh: 阿胡迭，長子。

translations.literal: Ahudie: eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Ahudie: eldest son.

sentences.zh: 骨赧，季也。

translations.literal: Gunuan: the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Gunuan: youngest child.

sentences.zh: 蒲陽溫，曰幼子。

translations.literal: Puyangwen: called the youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Puyangwen: the youngest son.

sentences.zh: 益都，次第之通稱。

translations.literal: Yidu: a general term for order of birth.
translations.idiomatic: Yidu: general term for birth order.

sentences.zh: 第九曰「烏也」，十六曰「女魯歡」。

translations.literal: The ninth is called "Wuye"; the sixteenth is called "Nuluhuan."
translations.idiomatic: The ninth son is Wuye; the sixteenth is Nuluhuan.

sentences.zh: 按答海，客之通稱。

translations.literal: Andahai: a general term for a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Andahai: guest.

sentences.zh: 山只昆，舍人也。

translations.literal: Shanzhikun: a house servant.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhikun: house servant.

sentences.zh: 散亦孛，奇男子。

translations.literal: Sanyibo: an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Sanyibo: extraordinary man.

sentences.zh: 散答，老人之稱也。

translations.literal: Sanda: a term for an old man.
translations.idiomatic: Sanda: old man.

sentences.zh: 什古乃，瘠人。

translations.literal: Shigunai: a lean person.
translations.idiomatic: Shigunai: lean person.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦，黧黑之名。

translations.literal: Sahelian: a name for dark black.
translations.idiomatic: Sahelian: dark black.

sentences.zh: 保活里，侏儒。

translations.literal: Baohuoli: a dwarf.
translations.idiomatic: Baohuoli: dwarf.

sentences.zh: 阿里孫，貌不揚也。

translations.literal: Alisun: one of uncomely appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Alisun: plain-looking person.

sentences.zh: 阿徒罕，采薪之子。

translations.literal: Atuhan: a firewood-gathering lad.
translations.idiomatic: Atuhan: lad who gathers firewood.

sentences.zh: 答不也，耘田者。

translations.literal: Dabuye: a field-tiller.
translations.idiomatic: Dabuye: field-tiller.

sentences.zh: 阿土古，善採捕者。

translations.literal: Atugu: one skilled at hunting and trapping.
translations.idiomatic: Atugu: skilled hunter.

sentences.zh: 阿里喜，圍獵也。

translations.literal: Alixi: encircling hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Alixi: encircling hunt.

sentences.zh: 拔里速，角牴戲者。

translations.literal: Balisu: a wrestler.
translations.idiomatic: Balisu: wrestler.

sentences.zh: 阿離合懣，臂鷹鶻者。

translations.literal: Alihemen: one who carries a hawk on the arm.
translations.idiomatic: Alihemen: falconer.

sentences.zh: 胡魯剌，戶長。

translations.literal: Hulula: household head.
translations.idiomatic: Hulula: household head.

sentences.zh: 阿合，人奴也。

translations.literal: Ahe: a human slave.
translations.idiomatic: Ahe: human slave.

sentences.zh: 兀朮，曰頭。

translations.literal: Wuzhu: called the head.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu: the head.

sentences.zh: 粘罕，心也。

translations.literal: Nianhan: the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Nianhan: the heart.

sentences.zh: 畏可，牙，又曰吾亦可。

translations.literal: Weike: tooth; also called Wuyeke.
translations.idiomatic: Weike: tooth; also Wuyeke.

sentences.zh: 盤里合，將指。

translations.literal: Panlihe: the general's finger.
translations.idiomatic: Panlihe: the general's finger.

sentences.zh: 三合，人之靨也。

translations.literal: Sanhe: a person's dimples.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhe: dimples.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔，瘍瘡。

translations.literal: Yawuta: ulcer and sore.
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta: ulcer or sore.

sentences.zh: 蒲剌都，目赤而盲也。

translations.literal: Puladu: eyes red and blind.
translations.idiomatic: Puladu: red-eyed and blind.

sentences.zh: 石哥里，溲疾。

translations.literal: Shigel: urinary ailment.
translations.idiomatic: Shigel: urinary disorder.

sentences.zh: 謾都謌，癡騃之謂。

translations.literal: Manduge: a term for stupidity and dullness.
translations.idiomatic: Manduge: stupidity.

sentences.zh: 謀良虎，無賴之名。

translations.literal: Moulianghu: a name for a rogue.
translations.idiomatic: Moulianghu: rogue.

sentences.zh: 皆不美之稱也。

translations.literal: All are terms of ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: All are unflattering names.

sentences.zh: 與人同受福曰「忽都」。

translations.literal: Sharing blessing with others is called "Hudu."
translations.idiomatic: Sharing good fortune with others: Hudu.

sentences.zh: 以力助人曰「阿息保」。

translations.literal: Helping others by force is called "Axibao."
translations.idiomatic: Helping others by strength: Axibao.

sentences.zh: 辭不失，酒醒也。

translations.literal: Cibushi: sober after wine.
translations.idiomatic: Cibushi: sober after drinking.

sentences.zh: 奴申，和睦之義。

translations.literal: Nushen: the meaning of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Nushen: harmony.

sentences.zh: 訛出虎，寬容之名也。

translations.literal: Echuhu: a name signifying tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: Echuhu: tolerance.

sentences.zh: 賽里，安樂。

translations.literal: Saili: peace and joy.
translations.idiomatic: Saili: peace and joy.

sentences.zh: 迪古乃，來也。

translations.literal: Digunai: come.
translations.idiomatic: Digunai: to come.

sentences.zh: 撒八，迅速之義。

translations.literal: Saba: the meaning of swiftness.
translations.idiomatic: Saba: swiftness.

sentences.zh: 烏古出，方言曰再休，猶言再不復也。

translations.literal: Wuguchu: in the dialect called zaixiu, meaning "never again."
translations.idiomatic: Wuguchu: in dialect zaixiu, meaning never again.

sentences.zh: 凡事之先者曰「石倫」。

translations.literal: Whatever is first in any matter is called "Shilun."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever comes first: Shilun.

sentences.zh: 以物與人已然曰「阿里白」。

translations.literal: Giving something to someone after it is already done is called "Alibai."
translations.idiomatic: Giving after the fact is complete: Alibai.

sentences.zh: 吾里補，畜積之名。

translations.literal: Wulibu: a name for accumulated stores.
translations.idiomatic: Wulibu: accumulated stores.

sentences.zh: 習失，猶人云常川也。

translations.literal: Xishi: like what people call "constant flow."
translations.idiomatic: Xishi: as people say "constant flow."

sentences.zh: 凡市物已得曰「兀帶」，取以名子者，猶言貨取如物然也。

translations.literal: Whenever a market transaction is completed it is called "Wudai"; taking this as a child's name is like saying goods taken as if they were objects.
translations.idiomatic: A completed market deal: Wudai; as a child's name it means goods taken like merchandise.

sentences.zh: 兀典，明星。

translations.literal: Wudian: bright star.
translations.idiomatic: Wudian: bright star.

sentences.zh: 阿鄰，山。

translations.literal: Alin: mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Alin: mountain.

sentences.zh: 太神，高也。

translations.literal: Taishen: high.
translations.idiomatic: Taishen: high.

sentences.zh: 山之上銳者曰「哈丹」，坡陀曰「阿懶」，大而峻曰「斜魯」。

translations.literal: A sharp mountain peak is called "Hadan"; a slope is "Alan"; large and steep is "Xielu."
translations.idiomatic: A sharp peak: Hadan; a slope: Alan; large and steep: Xielu.

sentences.zh: 忒鄰，海也。

translations.literal: Teilin: sea.
translations.idiomatic: Teilin: sea.

sentences.zh: 沙忽帶，舟也。

translations.literal: Shahudai: boat.
translations.idiomatic: Shahudai: boat.

sentences.zh: 生鐵曰「斡論」，釜曰「闍母」，刃曰「斜烈」。

translations.literal: Raw iron is "Wolun"; cauldron is "Zhamu"; blade is "Xielie."
translations.idiomatic: Raw iron: Wolun; cauldron: Zhamu; blade: Xielie.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火者槌也。

translations.literal: Poluhuo is a mallet.
translations.idiomatic: Poluhuo: mallet.

sentences.zh: 金曰「桉春」。

translations.literal: Gold is called "Anchun."
translations.idiomatic: Gold: Anchun.

sentences.zh: 銀朮可，珠也。

translations.literal: Yinzhuke: pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzhuke: pearl.

sentences.zh: 布囊曰「蒲盧渾」，盆曰「阿里虎」，罐曰「活女」。

translations.literal: Cloth sack is "Puluhun"; basin is "Alihu"; jar is "Huonu."
translations.idiomatic: Cloth sack: Puluhun; basin: Alihu; jar: Huonu.

sentences.zh: 烏烈，草廩也。

translations.literal: Wulie: grass granary.
translations.idiomatic: Wulie: grass granary.

sentences.zh: 沙剌，衣襟也。

translations.literal: Shala: garment collar.
translations.idiomatic: Shala: garment collar.
